prs.title: fix(browser): treat edge as chromium in toHaveStyle
prs.author: aliamanatali
prs.body:
Edge is Chromium-based, so like Chrome it only computes styles for elements in the page's own document. It was missing from both checks and got the detached document, which left the expected styles empty.

Fixes #11668

prs.title: feat(experimental): add trace timeline for node
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- closes https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/11701
- follow-up to https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/11592

This PR adds `experimental.traceTimeline`, which records `expect.poll`, `vi.waitFor`, and `vi.waitUntil` steps in Node tests and prints the same timeline as browser mode (#11594) when a test fails. For example:

```
 FAIL  profile.test.js > loads profile
AssertionError: expected 3 to be 10 // Object.is equality
...

Trace:
  step                   start  duration  location
  vi.waitFor()            +0ms     101ms  profile.test.js:3:12
  expect.poll().toBe()  +305ms     501ms  profile.test.js:5:52
```

Some implementation details:

- Only failed attempts keep their steps, like the failure-only mode proposed in #10310, so the option adds almost no overhead to passing tests.
- Locations resolve like error stacks, so a step inside a helper file points at the helper, and a step inside `vi.defineHelper` points at the line that called the helper.
- The option has no effect in browser mode, which records its own steps with `browser.traceView`.
- `vi.waitFor` and `vi.waitUntil` are attributed to the test from `getCurrentTest()`, and are skipped while several tests run concurrently by checking `getRunningTests().size > 1` to avoid false trace attribution.

prs.title: refactor(snapshot): unify review update with `SnapshotState` update
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- follow-up to https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11325

Previously, the interactive review in #11325 rebuilt each update from the serialized test error (trimmed `actual`, `meta`, `stacks[0]`), even though `SnapshotState` already knew what the update should be for `--update`. The divergence can cause minor differences in how `--update` and review mode apply updates.

This PR makes `SnapshotState` return the update it would write under `--update`, so that the snapshot review can reuse it.

prs.title: refactor: share trace types and utils
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- follow-up to https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11594
- follow-up to https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11753

The trace types lived in the browser package, and the logic that merges trace entries lived in the UI. The terminal timeline (#11594) copied both into `vitest`'s reporter, and the node trace timeline (#11753) copied the types again into the runtime.

This PR finally unifies the utilities into `@vitest/utils/trace`, which is consumed by `ui`, `browser`, and `vitest`. This resolves the TODOs these PRs left about sharing the types.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Trace data types (`BrowserTraceData`, `BrowserTraceEntry`, `BrowserTraceSnapshot`, `BrowserTraceEntryStatus`) | `packages/browser/src/client/tester/trace.ts`, imported by the UI through a relative path, and copied in `vitest`'s reporter and runtime | `@vitest/utils/trace` |
| `BrowserTraceEntryKind` | `packages/vitest/src/public/browser.ts` | `@vitest/utils/trace`, still exported from `vitest/browser` |
| Merging trace artifacts by attempt and pairing range start/end entries | `packages/ui/client/composables/trace-view.ts`, copied in `vitest`'s reporter | `groupTraceAttempts` in `@vitest/utils/trace` |

prs.title: fix(vm): keep assignable accessor globals writable in node environment
prs.author: MO2k4
prs.body:
### Description

Written by an AI agent (Claude) on behalf of @MO2k4, who has reviewed it.

The `node` environment's `setupVM()` installs missing host globals as lazy accessors. On first read the getter swaps itself for a data property and copies `writable` from the host descriptor. For an accessor that is `undefined`, so the global becomes read-only even when the host accessor has a setter. On Node 25+ `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` are such accessors, and reading one before assigning it throws `TypeError: Cannot redefine property` under `vmThreads` and `vmForks`.

A host accessor with a setter now stays writable. This also covers `performance`, so its special case is removed. Getter-only accessors such as `navigator` and `crypto` stay read-only.

The new test reads and then assigns `performance`, `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` in both vm pools. It fails on main under Node 26 with the error above.

Resolves #11833

prs.title: fix: rerun on file changes after a config restart (fix #11772)
prs.author: magurotuna
prs.body:
Fixes #11772

### Problem

In watch mode, if I save `vitest.config.ts`, Vitest runs all tests once. After that, Vitest never runs tests again, even when I save a test file or a source file.

### Cause

When a file changes, the watcher first adds the affected test files to `changedTests`. Then it schedules a rerun. The rerun runs those files and clears `changedTests`. If a file is already in `changedTests`, `handleFileChanged` ignores the change, because a rerun is already scheduled.

A config change does two things at once. First, the watcher adds every test file to `changedTests` and schedules a rerun. Second, Vitest restarts, and the restart cancels that scheduled rerun. So nothing clears `changedTests`, and the set still has every test file after the restart.

As a result, `handleFileChanged` ignores every later change. It expects a rerun that will never come.

### Fix

When the restart cancels the scheduled rerun, it now also clears `changedTests` and `invalidates`.

### Test

The new test saves the config file and waits for the restart. Then it saves a source file and waits for the rerun. Without the fix, the test times out on the last wait.
